name: Hittite Empire (Muwatalli II)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 250,000-350,000 km2 at 1300 and 300,000-400,000 km2 at 1200 BCE; Taagepera 1978 gives 0.45 million km2 for 1250-1220 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). The historical-basemaps world_bc1500 'Hittites' polygon (central Anatolia to Ugarit and Carchemish; bc1500 is the nearest file at or before 1274) measures ~412,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON.

population.note: Seshat codes 1,300,000-2,000,000 for the New Kingdom of Hatti (1400-1180 BCE). Bryce 2024 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) gives 'more than 200,000' and Zsolt Simon 140,000-150,000 for the kingdom; those figures cover Hatti proper only and are incompatible with the 47,500-man Kadesh army unless the vassal kingdoms are counted, so they are excluded. Range includes the Syrian and western Anatolian vassals inside the border.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Hattusa itself may have held only 2,300-4,600 people (Seeher via Bryce, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites); Seshat codes the largest settlement at 15,000-20,000. Syrian cities (Ugarit, Carchemish, Aleppo) were larger.

activePersonnel.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Mid = the Kadesh army (~47,500 incl. crews) as the standing order of battle at campaign start; low = Holmes' 15,000 infantry plus chariot crews; high adds garrisons against the Kaska and in the west.

trainedReserves.note: Bryce: up to ~100,000 could be called for military service, incl. labour; reserves callable within a month are a fraction of that. Estimate.

supportPersonnel.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Chariot crews: 2,500-3,500 vehicles x 3 men (Healy 9,000-11,100) minus the infantry rider counted nowhere else, plus logistics.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Feudal service obligations of land holders and vassal treaties requiring contingents; Bryce's 100,000 for service against a ~1.6 M empire is ~6%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Split: close-order spear and sickle-sword infantry, Hittite and vassal ~71% of the foot.

quality.note: Bronze spears and sickle swords, helmets; era-typical.

training.note: Core Hittite troops professional (0.75), vassal contingents levies.

count.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Split: archers ~10% of the foot (Hittite infantry were mainly spearmen).

Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Split: light vassal and highland troops, skirmishers ~19% of the foot.

Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Low 2,000 allows for the ~2,000 Hittite vehicles the Egyptians claim destroyed being an exaggeration; mid between Healy's 2,500 and the Egyptian 3,500; crews in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Heavier three-man chariot with spearman, built for shock; among the era's best.

training.note: Professional chariot corps; the Kadesh charge broke the Ra division.

count.note: Hittite naval power was the fleet of the vassal Ugarit: Ugaritic text KTU 2.47 refers to 150 ships from Ugarit (Wachsmann 1999, note 19, fetched); not all were warships. Not at Kadesh. Estimate.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Muwatalli concealed a large army behind Kadesh and caught Ramesses with false intelligence; a well-run campaign, though the chariot attack lost cohesion while looting.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: multi-vassal coalition held by treaties; Hittite core more cohesive.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: defending the Syrian frontier at the peak of power.

weapons.note: Anchor 2: composite bow, heavy three-man chariot, bronze swords; iron objects were rare prestige items.

armor.note: Anchor 2: bronze scale for chariot crews, helmets.

ships.note: Below anchor 2: a land power relying on the Ugaritic vassal fleet.

fortification.note: Above anchor 2: Hattusa's double stone walls with towers, postern tunnels, stone citadels.

logistics.note: Anchor 2: granaries (Hattusa silos), ox wagons, vassal supply.

communications.note: Anchor 2: couriers and the diplomatic letter network.

isr.note: Anchor 2: effective deception and scouting at Kadesh.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Turkey 1 CE = 897, 1000 CE = 768 (2011 int$). The dry-farming plateau was poorer than the irrigated valleys; Syrian vassals richer.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Chronic frontier war with the Kaska and Egypt.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Metal working, chariot building; agrarian base.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Dry farming on the plateau; large state grain silos at Hattusa (capacity for tens of thousands).

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; Bronze Age life expectancy was if anything lower, so this is not an underestimate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Hittite route network between Hattusa and the provinces; little engineered paving.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Ugarit, Ura in Cilicia and other vassal harbours.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Kadesh campaign marched ~800 km from Hattusa through vassal territory with vassal supply.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, donkeys, chariot horses; ~0.12-0.16 per inhabitant on an agro-pastoral plateau.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: plateau with mountain approaches, fortified capital, harsh winters.

notes: Snapshot = May 1274 BCE, Muwatalli II at Kadesh. Forces = the coalition army at campaign start (Hittite plus vassal contingents), as the empire's population convention includes the vassal kingdoms inside the bc1500 polygon. Population estimates disagree by an order of magnitude (Bryce/Simon for Hatti proper vs Seshat for the empire); see the population note. Egyptian figures (37,000 infantry, 3,500 chariots) appear only as the high bound.
